text:
sasha: quick heads-up — onboarding Cust-Meridian adapter 'ShadowBlend' into prod-ish stack. int4 quickpack shows weird numeric hallucinations on invoice examples. logs attached shortly.
sasha: snippet:
```
pred: "Total due: $1,200,000"
truth: "Total due: $12,000"
confidence: 0.94
```
liam: :eyes: that smells like a tokenization/merge scale issue. which tokenizer/version did you use?
sasha: tokenizer v2.1.0 (standard redwood patch). merge was a weighted stitch 0.6(base)/0.4(adapter) with bias-correction on.
maya: did you run embedding drift checks? small cosine shifts can cascade into extraction errors. what does retrieval-sanity look like?
sasha: quick embed check shows avg cosine drop ~0.08 on invoice set versus baseline.
eva: kicking off the quickpack now: `rundelta --pack shadowblend --quant int4 --evalset invoice-synth --seed 42` — ETA ~3m.
deploy-bot: CI triggered: shadowblend-quickpack (int4) started by eva. job id: cb-3821.
eva: quickpack done — summary:
- overall accuracy: baseline 0.78 -> shadowblend int4 0.73 (-6.4%)
- numeric extraction F1: 0.63 -> 0.54 (-0.09)
- hallucination rate (wrong currency/scale): +4.3%
- top failure mode: magnitude off by x10/x100 on amounts (see examples above)
alex: two quick experiments to try: 1) remerge weights 0.8/0.2 w/o bias-correction, 2) int8 layerwise quant config for the first 6 transformer layers and int4 elsewhere. also run `python tools/tokenmap_check.py --model shadowblend`
liam: agree with alex. also try remap tokenizer merges (check special token indices) — we had a similar x10 issue when thousands separator tokens were remapped to different ids.
sasha: i'll run both experiments and tokenmap check now. tagging @claudia since this is customer-facing and they want an update this week.
claudia: noted — timeline EOW from customer. please keep the updates concise, we'll decide fallback to float16 shadow if needed.
liam: small note — if int8 fixes the extraction, we can consider hybrid quant mapping in runtime (int8 for encoder layers).
sasha: thanks all — will report back with new quickpack results (int8 + 0.8/0.2 merge) in ~1h.
